Something like: "Human beings who eat certain (ie not junk food or nutritionally inadequate) vegan diets live longer and have lower rates of the particular diseases (the ones which most plague mankind and also happen to be diet related: cardiovascular disease, etc.)" Or more simplified, perhaps: "Humans thrive best on whole food plant-based vegan diets."

Also, the conclusion is framed from the carnist perspective. First, the verb "produce" is actually serving here as a euphemism for exploitation. Production of animal products always involves killing an animal who desires to avoid pain and continue living, and usually involves rape, mutilation, imprisonment, and torture as well. Secondly, our role as abolitionists is to advocate for the animals who are victims of injustice. An "animal product" cannot be a victim because a product is an inanimate thing which is dead and cannot suffer. Finally, we want the audience to reach a vegan conclusion, yet the way the conclusion is currently phrased gives them an excuse not to change (which happens to be a very common excuse: "it's necessary"). But the reality is that it is absolutely unnecessary for me to produce or support the production of animal products (my very existence as a vegan is proof of this). Our goal is to persuade the audience that the same is true for them as well.

Perhaps something like "It is unethical to use animals for human entertainment, clothing, or food." would be much closer to the conclusion I'd like the audience to reach. This phrasing emphasizes that vegans are not talking about "food" but the abolition of exploitation of animals in all forms.
